4.3 . Reinforcement learning algorithm
A DDPG framework with four deep neural networks—two actor and two critic networks—is used for the RL algorithm. The deep neural network structures are presented in Fig. 3.
The actor deep neural network takes observations as input and expands the hidden layer through two fully connected (FC) and Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU) layers. The output 𝐴(𝑡) is resized by an FC layer, and a hyperbolic tangent function scales its amplitude. The critic deep neural network has two inputs: the observation is expanded through an FC-ReLU layer and regulated to the same dimension as the expanded action by an FC layer. Then the two layers are summed to obtain a new combined layer. The criticism is further calculated by a combined ReLU-FC layer. The DL networks are trained with 24-hour data of the

5 . Numerical experiments
The proposed RLEMS is validated in the environment shown in Fig. 1. The configuration of the MG is presented in Table 2. Constraints for the
S o C _ { B }
are defined to prolong the lifecycle of the battery. The residential loads include a coffee machine, refrigerators, ovens, TVs, workstations, laptops, and some cooking staff. The appliances are used randomly by the user working in the laboratory. In this way, the uncertainty from user actions is introduced into the validation. The uncertainty from the renewable generation and energy market is introduced by the realistic data of PV power and energy prices. The experimental dataset is pre-sented in Fig. 4. The feasibility of the proposed RLEMS is verified in both winter and summer scenarios. The winter case is shown in Fig. 4(a), which indicates a high energy price and low PV generation.
